board_entry: confirmation standard (blocker) / BEST GRADIENT-FREE POINT / B-ROUTE (key side)
question: PLAN_AM_MUST_WIN.md §3 requires every reported result to be reproduced WITH A CHANGED SEED, and DIAG-KEYCURVE proved by direct test that no seed knob reaches the per-document AM write (config.seed never reaches the per_document path; cartridges/am/continual.py:150 seeds the reference draw with the constant doc_idx). (A) Build a minimal, opt-in, default-preserving seed knob. (B) Using it, does the mission's best point -- MECH-005 keys+reposition at its k=12 minimum, QA 1.9560 / MT 2.2720 -- and in particular its keys-vs-control dMT of ~-0.20, survive seed variation?
variable_under_test: AM_SEED_OFFSET in {0, 1000, 2000} -- i.e. WHICH 32 of each document's ~500 reference conversations the closed-form solve is fitted to. Everything else held at the MECH-005 configuration (KEY_MODE=highest_attention, AM_KEY_REPOSITION=1, AM_ROPE_THETA=5000000, ENABLE_BETA=0, TOP_T=32, GRANULARITY=per_layer, SLOT_SELECTION=tfidf, USE_IDF=0, RIDGE_LAMBDA=1e-4, RIDGE_SCALE=spectral, DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2, MAX_QUERIES_PER_HEAD=64) and, for the mechanism-off control, the same config with KEY_MODE=freeze and AM_KEY_REPOSITION unset.

numbers._note: qa/mt are the MEAN over the three seed offsets {0,1000,2000} of the keys arm at its k=12 minimum (per-offset QA 1.9560121/1.9397202/1.9446365, MT 2.2720184/2.2695382/2.2626297). solve_s is the mean AM Phase-2 wall clock of the three keys runs (296.2/296.8/310.5); phase2_e2e_s is the mean end-to-end wall clock including model load and in-run evals (487/437/669). The control's solve_s is 157.4/164.7 s.

PART_A_default_preservation.method: three runs of the identical keys+reposition configuration: A1 = `git archive HEAD` snapshot (/tmp/amsnap_mechseed, no seed_offset field at all), A2 = edited working tree with AM_SEED_OFFSET UNSET, A3 = edited working tree with AM_SEED_OFFSET=0 explicit. sha256 of all 16 per-document `cache-after-doc-*.pt` snapshots + `cache_last.pt` (17 artefacts) compared across the three.
PART_A_default_preservation.config_yaml_diff_note: the ONLY difference is the new field serialising at its default. Adding a pydantic field necessarily adds one line to config.yaml; no numerical artefact differs.

PART_A_knob_is_not_cosmetic.method: CPU probe (seed_offset_probe.py) replaying `group_conversations_by_document` -> `limit_conversations(..., seed=doc_idx+offset)` on the real MT parquet (16 documents, 8192 conversations), cross-checked against the library function by object identity.
PART_A_knob_is_not_cosmetic.plain_statement: a non-zero offset replaces ~30 of each document's 32 reference conversations; 0 of 16 documents keep the same draw.

adversarial_worst_case_pairing.note: keys' WORST seed against the control's BEST seed at matched k -- the least favourable pairing the data allows.
adversarial_worst_case_pairing.verdict: both dMT still clear the 0.15 band; neither dQA does.

effect_vs_seed_noise.plain_statement: the seed-to-seed spread of the point under test is one to two ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE smaller than the keys-vs-control MT effect. The effect is not a seed artefact.

internals_per_run.note: `ref_mass_on_S` is the solve-time attention mass on the written slots (mean over layers and documents), from `am_stats.extra.ref_mass_on_S_per_layer`. The keys arm carries 2.4-2.5x the control's solve-time mass at every seed, exactly as at offset 0 -- the mechanism's internal signature is seed-stable too.

vs_mission_target.verdict: QA clears the budget at every seed; MT falls ~0.25 short at every seed. NOT a mission PASS.

confirmation_standard_checklist_PLAN_§3.fresh_process_reproduction: DONE -- A2 reproduces the k=12 and k=16 numbers to all 16 printed digits; A1/A2/A3 are byte-identical over 17 cartridge artefacts.
confirmation_standard_checklist_PLAN_§3.changed_seed: DONE -- two non-zero offsets (1000, 2000), both splits, both k, plus the mechanism-off control at both offsets.
confirmation_standard_checklist_PLAN_§3.mechanism_off_ablation: DONE, and seed-varied: KEY_MODE=freeze at offsets 0/1000/2000, same session, same harness.
confirmation_standard_checklist_PLAN_§3.phase1_floor_control: DONE -- untouched Phase-1 cartridge re-evaluated in this session: QA 2.23880672454834 / MT 3.7825491428375244, exact to 16 digits.

cross_check_against_workers_that_finishe.note: DIAG-CONTROLCURVE and DIAG-NOISE completed while this job was on GPU 1. Both change how the numbers above should be read, so they are recorded here rather than left for the orchestrator to notice.

DIAG-NOISE_measured_resolution.implication_for_this_result: keys-vs-control at matched k is a PAIRED comparison (same eval examples, same session), so 0.0494 is the applicable MT yardstick. Every per-seed dMT reported here (0.176-0.321) is 3.6-6.5x that resolution, and even the adversarial worst-case pairing (-0.1519) clears it by 3.1x. Against the composite 0.1055 all six dMT still clear. The dQA values (0.112-0.231) sit at or below the QA composite resolution 0.1967 at k=12, so the QA verdict is unchanged.
DIAG-NOISE_measured_resolution.independent_corroboration: this job's own measurement of seed variance -- keys k=12 MT range 0.0094 over three offsets -- is itself 5x SMALLER than DIAG-NOISE's paired MT resolution, i.e. the seed is not even the dominant noise term in this comparison.

DIAG-CONTROLCURVE_relocated_the_control_.STRONGEST_SURVIVING_OBJECTION: This job verified the MATCHED-k comparison (k=12 and k=16) across seeds, and there the dMT is large and robust. It did NOT verify the OWN-OPTIMUM comparison, because only k=12 and k=16 were evaluated at the non-zero offsets. DIAG-CONTROLCURVE, evaluating all 16 control k at offset 0, found the control's true MT minimum at k=10 (2.4083, not the k=8 2.4536 DIAG-KEYCURVE had assumed), which shrinks the own-optimum dMT to -0.1363 and the own-optimum dQA to -0.0115. So: 'keys beat frozen keys at matched k' is now seed-confirmed; 'keys beat frozen keys when each arm is allowed its own best k' is a different, weaker claim that this job did not test and that DIAG-CONTROLCURVE reports as much closer to the resolution limit. Anyone quoting the -0.21 must say which comparison it is.

eval_provenance.eval_hang_handling: every eval was launched in the background, polled for the `Eval loss - ` line, then SIGTERM/SIGKILLed (RUNBOOK §1).

command: FILES EDITED (uncommitted, MECH-007): cartridges/am/finetune.py (+13, `seed_offset: int = 0` on AttentionMatchingFinetuningConfig), cartridges/am/continual.py (+34, reads the offset via getattr with a fail-loud >=0 check and uses `draw_seed = doc_idx + seed_offset` for BOTH `limit_conversations` and `build_reference_dataloader`; records the offset in the aggregate only when non-zero), examples/qasper2/train/continual_am_sparse.py (+45, `AM_SEED_OFFSET` env var + `_seed_offset_kwargs()` conditional-kwarg helper wired into `_build_am_config`). RUN: `nohup bash research_loop/results/MECH-SEED/launch_mech_seed.sh &` then `research_loop/results/MECH-SEED/finalize.py`. CPU sanity: `research_loop/results/MECH-SEED/seed_offset_probe.py` + a 6-case config-construction matrix.
observations: 1) THE SEED KNOB IS BUILT AND IS BIT-IDENTICAL WHEN DEFAULT, PROVEN TWO WAYS. Three runs of the identical keys+reposition configuration -- (A1) the `git archive HEAD` snapshot, which has no `seed_offset` field at all, (A2) the edited working tree with AM_SEED_OFFSET unset, (A3) the edited working tree with AM_SEED_OFFSET=0 explicit -- produce sha256-identical output over all 17 cartridge artefacts (16 per-document snapshots + cache_last.pt), identical `am/mean_mse` (0.0039414096599943195), identical `|v|max` (78.5) and identical in-run evals (QA 2.0349531173706055 / MT 2.3290133476257324). The only difference anywhere is one line in config.yaml, `seed_offset: 0`, which is the new field serialising at its default. 2) THE KNOB IS NOT COSMETIC. A CPU probe replaying the actual draw on the real MT parquet shows a non-zero offset replaces ~30 of each document's 32 reference conversations: mean shared 2.19/32 (offset 1000) and 2.63/32 (offset 2000), mean Jaccard 0.036 / 0.043, and 0 of 16 documents keep the same draw. Both consumers of the per-document seed are offset together (`limit_conversations`, which chooses WHICH conversations, and `build_reference_dataloader`, which seeds the packing/ordering); the old-reference-guard bank at continual.py:75 uses a fixed seed=0 and is untouched because it is not per-document and is off by default. 3) THE OFFSET-0 GATE PASSED EXACTLY: QA 1.9560121297836304 / MT 2.2720184326171875 at k=12 and QA 2.034916400909424 / MT 2.330503463745117 at k=16, to all 16 printed digits. So did the same-session mechanism-off control (2.074141263961792 / 2.4704575538635254 at k=12; 2.159724712371826 / 2.529625177383423 at k=16) and the Phase-1 floor (QA 2.23880672454834 / MT 3.7825491428375244). 4) THE POINT ITSELF IS REMARKABLY SEED-STABLE. Keys arm at k=12 over offsets {0,1000,2000}: MT 2.27202 / 2.26954 / 2.26263, mean 2.26806, RANGE 0.0094; QA 1.95601 / 1.93972 / 1.94464, mean 1.94679, range 0.0163. At k=16: MT mean 2.30895 range 0.0404; QA mean 2.01116 range 0.0388. The control is noisier -- k=12 MT range 0.0677, k=16 MT range 0.1290, the largest single spread observed and close to the noise band. 5) THE KEYS-VS-CONTROL dMT SURVIVES SEED VARIANCE, AND NOT MARGINALLY. At matched k=12 the per-offset dMT is -0.1984 / -0.1791 / -0.2537 (mean -0.2104, range 0.0746); at k=16 it is -0.1991 / -0.1761 / -0.3212 (mean -0.2322, range 0.1451). All six deltas have the same sign and all six exceed the 0.15 band. Even the adversarial pairing -- the keys arm's WORST seed against the control's BEST seed -- gives -0.1766 at k=12 and -0.1519 at k=16, both still outside the band. The effect is 22x the keys arm's own across-seed spread at k=12 and 3.1x the larger of the two arms' spreads there. 6) THE QA-SIDE CLAIM REMAINS UNCONFIRMED, exactly as DIAG-KEYCURVE's correction said. dQA at k=12 is -0.1181 / -0.1125 / -0.1262 (mean -0.1189): consistently negative, consistently INSIDE the +-0.15 band at every seed. At k=16 the mean is -0.1658 but only the offset-2000 arm clears the band (-0.2305 vs -0.1248 / -0.1420). Adversarially paired, dQA is -0.0962 (k=12) and -0.1032 (k=16), well inside the band. So: the MT advantage is confirmed, the QA advantage is not. 7) THE INTERNAL SIGNATURE IS SEED-STABLE TOO: solve-time `ref_mass_on_S` is 0.3136 / 0.3615 / 0.3587 for the keys arm and 0.1452 / 0.1460 for the control -- a 2.4-2.5x ratio at every seed -- while `am/mean_mse` is 0.00394 / 0.00353 / 0.00348 (keys) vs 0.01424 / 0.01353 (control) and `|v|max` 78.5 / 77.0 / 88.0 vs 139 / 162. Solve cost is 296-311 s for the keys arm vs 157-165 s for the control, i.e. the mechanism costs ~1.9x, seed-independent. 8) AGAINST THE MISSION BAR THIS IS STILL NOT A PASS. Averaged over seeds the best point is QA 1.9468 / MT 2.2681: it clears the QA budget (<=2.52) by 0.573 at every seed but falls 0.248 SHORT of the MT target (<=2.02) at every seed, best seed included (2.2626, short by 0.243). All four elements of PLAN §3's confirmation standard are now satisfied for this point -- fresh-process reproduction (byte-identical), changed seed (two non-zero offsets), the mechanism-off ablation (seed-varied), and the Phase-1 floor control (re-run in-session, exact) -- but §3's PASS threshold is not. 9) PROVENANCE: repo HEAD e992ac35 unchanged before and after; snapshot manifest sha256 13babff8c3... identical at launch and after; A1 ran from the snapshot (which contains zero occurrences of `seed_offset`) while A2/A3/B1-B4 ran from the working tree (3 occurrences); the runs that were given a flag logged the `MECH-007:` line that exists only in the edited driver, and the two flag-unset runs logged nothing. One GPU claimed via flock (gpu1) for the whole job while DIAG-CONTROLCURVE held gpu0 with its own pinned snapshot. All 26 evals were verified to have loaded the checkpoint they were given (fixed-string grep of each eval log), and every eval was killed after its `Eval loss` line per RUNBOOK §1. 10) CAVEATS I DID NOT ARGUE AWAY: the eval sets are fixed and tiny (MT n=69 / QA n=78), so three seeds give three samples of a coarse instrument and the ranges quoted are ranges of three, not confidence intervals. The seed variation implemented perturbs ONE stochastic choice -- which reference conversations each document contributes -- because that is the only one the per-document AM path has; it does NOT vary document order, slot selection (deterministic given the draw), or eval sampling, so it is a lower bound on total run-to-run variance. Only k=12 and k=16 were evaluated at the non-zero offsets, so each arm's per-seed argmin over k is unlocated and the 'own-optimum' comparison could not be recomputed under seed variation. The control's k=16 MT spread (0.129) is itself near the noise band, which is the single largest source of uncertainty in the reported dMT. 11) TWO WORKERS FINISHED DURING THIS RUN AND BOTH BEAR ON THE VERDICT. DIAG-NOISE measured the harness resolution directly: MT paired 95% = 0.0494, MT composite 95% = 0.1055, i.e. the RUNBOOK's +-0.15 rule was too wide for paired comparisons. Keys-vs-control at matched k IS a paired comparison, so every per-seed dMT here (0.176-0.321) is 3.6-6.5x the applicable resolution, and this job's own seed-variance measurement (keys k=12 MT range 0.0094) is 5x SMALLER than that resolution -- the seed is not even the dominant noise term. Under the tighter yardstick the dQA at k=12 (0.112-0.126) still sits below the QA composite resolution of 0.1967, so the QA verdict does not change. DIAG-CONTROLCURVE mapped all 16 control k and relocated the control's true MT minimum to k=10 (MT 2.4083), not the k=8 that DIAG-KEYCURVE could only bound; that shrinks the OWN-OPTIMUM dMT to -0.1363 and dQA to -0.0115. THIS IS THE STRONGEST SURVIVING OBJECTION TO MY RESULT AND I DID NOT TEST IT: I verified the matched-k comparison across seeds, not the own-optimum one, because only k=12 and k=16 were evaluated at the non-zero offsets. 'Keys beat frozen keys at matched k' is now seed-confirmed and comfortably outside the measured resolution; 'keys beat frozen keys when each arm is allowed its own best k' is a weaker, untested-under-seed claim that DIAG-CONTROLCURVE puts much closer to the limit. Any quotation of -0.21 must say which of the two comparisons it is.
